title: Ending a Personal Services Plan — Cancellation Notice and the End of a Residency
content:
A Personal Services Plan ends in one of two ways: by the resident's signed cancellation, or because the resident's Larkspur residency has ended. The Resident and Family Services desk applies these rules.

## Cancellation by the resident

- **End date by signing day.** A resident cancels a plan by signed cancellation. Signed on or before the tier's cancellation cutoff day of a month, the plan ends on the last day of that month; signed later, on the last day of the following month.
- **Minimum commitment.** A package cancellation may not end the plan before the tier's minimum commitment months have run from the plan's effective date; the end date is then the last day of the month in which the commitment is completed.
- **Withdrawal.** A cancellation may be withdrawn before its end date, and the plan continues unchanged.

| Cancellation signed on (cutoff on the 20th for every tier) | Plan ends, subject to the minimum commitment |
|---|---|
| 1st to 20th of a month | Last day of that month |
| 21st to the last day of a month | Last day of the following month |

*Hypothetical:* a cancellation signed on 20 September ends a plan, whose commitment has already run, on 30 September; signed on 21 September, it ends the plan on 31 October.

## End of the residency

- When the resident's independent living or assisted living residency ends, the plan ends on that residency's fee end date, without notice or commitment.
- The package fee for the days after that date is credited where the tier prorates the package fee on the end of a residency.
- A plan whose residency has ended may be ended without the resident's signature, on the strength of the residency record.

## Points of judgement

- The residency-end route rests on the residency record held for the resident; neither the cancellation notice cutoff nor the minimum commitment applies to it.
- A package cancellation signed by the resident is subject both to the signing-day rule and to the minimum commitment clause.
